content: 1. Deutetrabenazine and primaquine both have the potential to increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, coadministration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 2. Dolasetron and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 3. Donepezil and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 4. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, efavirenz and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 5. Elagolix decreases the levels of primaquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered, and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 6. Primaquine and eliglustat both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 7. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of primaquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. 8. Encorafenib affects hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Primaquine and escitalopram both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 10. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 11. Primaquine increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 12. Fingolimod and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 13. Primaquine and flecainide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 14. Primaquine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if coadministered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Primaquine and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 16. Primaquine and fluoxetine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 17. Primaquine and fluphenazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 18. Primaquine and fluvoxamine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 19. Primaquine and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 20. Gemifloxacin and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 21. Gilteritinib and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 22. Primaquine and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Obtain ECGs when initiating therapy, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold therapy if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 23. Primaquine and goserelin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 24. Granisetron and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 25. Primaquine and haloperidol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 26. Primaquine and histrelin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 27. Hydroxyzine and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 28. Ifosfamide and primaquine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Ifosfamide may enhance the toxicities of myelosuppressive agents. Monitor for increased risk of myelosuppression. 29. Iloperidone increases the levels of primaquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 30. Primaquine increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting hepatic CYP2E1 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 31. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 32. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, itraconazole and primaquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 33. Primaquine and lapatinib both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 34. Primaquine increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended if coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 35. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Coadministration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure to midazolam, potentially prolonging sedation. 44.
